newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: U.N. envoy to try to end Brazzaville fighting.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy to try to end Brazzaville fighting.

text.p: United Nations envoy Mohamed Sahnoun arrived in Brazzaville on Thursday to try again to end fighting in the Congo Republic capital, U.N. sources said.
Sahnoun came by plane from Kinshasa, capital of the neighbouring Democratic Republic of the Congo across the river.
He was expected to try to bring together the rivals in the month-long conflict -- President Pascal Lissouba and his predecessor Denis Sassou Nguesso.
The veteran Algerian diplomat was also to meet Bernard Kolelas, mayor of Brazzaville, who chairs a committee trying to broker a deal, before leaving later on Thursday for Gabon.
Neighbouring Gabon's President Omar Bongo, a son-in-law of Sassou and friend of Lissouba, heads a separate international mediation committee.
"He (Sahnoun) will be doing the usual rounds, trying to meet with Sassou and Lissouba, and also Kolelas," a U.N. source said.
Kolelas failed on Wednesday to bring the rivals together for ceasefire talks, and firing was heard in Brazzaville on Wednesday night and Thursday morning.

Hundreds of people have been killed and whole districts of the city devastated. Fighting erupted after Lissouba's troops surrounded Sassou's home in a crackdown on private militia ahead of planned elections on July 27.
The International Committee of the Red Cross has sent aid to displaced people sheltering on an island on the Congo River between Kinshasa and Brazzaville.
